newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT-Dutch chartists divided on AEX index trend.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dutch chartists divided on AEX index trend.

text.p: Dutch chartists were much divided on the direction of the AEX index of leading shares, after last week's correction.

ING Barings said on Monday the AEX share index was expected to fall further after last week's correction, but ABN AMRO on the other hand said that the market was heavily oversold and waiting to bounce up again.
"Amsterdam has made a sharp correction within a longer term uptrend," ABN AMRO said. "We expect a renewed attack on the 750-level," it added.

Last week the AEX share index dropped 38.76 points to 727.30 and the index fell back another 11 points on Monday afternoon to 716.30, after hitting a day's low of 710.87 points earlier and tested 700 on Thursday.
"The selling condition of the AEX remains intact," said ING Barings.
MeesPierson also opted for the downtrend for this week, while contributors Jaad and Rabo Securities said that the index would stay neutral.

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.

ABN AMRO - Amsterdam has made a sharp correction within a longer term uptrend. The AEX has found support slightly above 700. Positive momentum will pick up again and we expect a renewed attack on the 750 level. In this market we prefer an aggressive approach and we advise to reopen long positions. This move up can take place on very short time frame. The market is heavily oversold and waiting to bounce up again. The old uptrend support line will now act as resistance.

ING BARINGS - The selling condition of the AEX remains intact. Intermediate resistance comes in at 735, then at 750. Both fast and slow momentum lines remain weak, confirming negative technicals. the Advance/Decline ratio of the Amsterdam stock market has been topping a bit in the past days, indicating weakening market breadth. it shows an increasing number of falling stocks. The money flow indicators have reversed their upward path in the past few days, suggesting some selling pressure coming in. We certainly do not rule out some strong rebounds, given recent oversold condition of the AEX.
But, we remain negative for the near future, and expect some volatile movements. Strong long-term support comes in at the levels of its 200-day moving average line around 675.

RABO SECURITIES - We expect highly volatile markets for this week. The AEX could easily test the rally low (700), but could just as easy look for resistance at 733 again. We expect the AEX to test support at 700 again before this correction is over and we therefore remain neutral.

MEESPIERSON - The momentum is showing divergence at very high levels and is still giving alarming signals. The blow off is still intact. Risks are on the downside. Trading range is expected to continue into this week with the 700 level supporting the downside and 748 as resistance. The short term trend is clearly down. The longer term is still a healthy uptrend.
